contexts.text: Temptation is straitness and anxiety from things which are repugnant to the loves.
A narrow chamber seen.
To straiten in all the gates () = to cut off all access to good and truth.
Straitness. Signified, Explained.

Jacob feared exceedingly, and he had distress () = the state, when it is being changed; (for) fear and straitness are the first thing of temptations; and they precede, when the state is being changed.
Hence the fear and straitness which precede spiritual temptation...
When the order is being inverted... the natural man is in fear and straitness. Explained.
Who answered me in the day of my distress () = in the state when he preferred truth before good.
He injected a painful contraction or straitness in the region of the lower belly.
When we saw the distress of his soul () = the state in which the internal is when it is estranged from the external. Explained.
Merely material things bear the lower mind downwards, thus into what is narrow.

For straitness of spirit () = on account of a state near despair... For they who are in this state are in straitness of spirit... That straitness of spirit is a state near despair, may be evident from the fact, that they who are in a state near despair are in internal anxiety, and are then actually in straitness of spirit. Straitness of spirit, in the external sense, is a compression of the breast, and a consequent kind of difficulty of breathing; but in the internal sense, it is anxiety on account of the deprivation of the truth of faith and the good of charity; and thus is a state near despair. Explained.
That the deprivation of spiritual truth and good gives birth to such anxiety, and consequently to such straitness, cannot be believed by those who are not in faith and charity. Fully explained.
To pass through the sea of straitness () = temptations. AE 654:24.
Straitness hath taken hold of us () = grief because truths were being infested.
There is no approach to any heavenly Society except through a narrow way...
The day of straitness, etc. = the advent of the Lord to Judgment.
Upon the earth distress of nations () = upon those who are in the Spiritual World.
Whom He hath redeemed out of the hand of the straitening enemy () = those whom He has delivered from falsities.
Behold straitness and thick darkness () = that (goods and truths) are nowhere to be found; but mere falsities...

Temptations themselves are signified by the bread of straitness, and the waters of oppression (). The bread of straitness = temptations as to the good of love... Straitness, and oppression = states of temptation.
A land of straitness and of anguish () = a Church where there will be no good of charity nor truth of faith.
But in straitness of times () = hardly and with difficulty, because with nations which have little perception of spiritual truth.
The rejection of good because of the evil which will then prevail in the Church... is signified by, there shall be great distress upon the land ().
Because such truth, like iron, is hard, shutting out and not admitting any genuine truth, it is said, that it may be for a siege, and thou shalt straiten it ().
That this was a grief of heart and mind... is signified by a day of straitness (). AE 721:26.
